decisionsTitle: The registrations Excel is live: colours as conditional formatting, the statistics as formulas (amending §172 and §787)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-16, from his phone:** «În excel export aș vrea color codes în funcție de status și dacă sunt membri BVR», and ten minutes later: «Dar statisticile din Excel trebuie să se actualizeze automat offline, gen să fie formule în Excel». **Amends §172** (the start list as a spreadsheet, `workbook.ts`) and **§787** (the statistics block under it).

**What the second sentence decides.** The file is the club's to edit after it leaves the application — fix a status, a sex, an age, untick a member — and it must stay right without the application. So nothing in it is a picture of the moment it was written: the colours are rules that read the cell's value, and the footer's numbers are formulas over the rows. A baked fill or a typed number would be right once and wrong at the first edit.

**Colours are conditional formatting, never a fill on a cell.** `sheet-colours.ts` writes `cfRule type="expression"` blocks over exactly the data rows (row 2 to the last registration; the header and the footer are outside), one per tint, each with its own differential format in `styles.xml`: `$M2="CONFIRMED"` and so on, with `OR(...)` for a tint that stands for several statuses. Edit a status and the row recolours; the status column still says the state in words, so colour is never the only way to read it. One map, `STATUS_TINT`, holds every status of the enum: confirmed `success` (pale green), a pending state or an offered place `warning` (pale yellow, as the desk's chip), the waiting list `info` (pale sky blue), cancelled and expired `neutral` (pale grey). **Never red:** the desk's chip uses the error colour for a cancelled or expired registration, but a whole red row shouts across a list of two hundred, so the sheet softens it. The header keeps its bold and has no fill. The palette is `SHEET_TINT` in `theme/brand.ts`, the one file a hex may live in (`colour-literals.test.ts`), and `brand`-side tests hold black ink on every tint above 4.5:1.

**The club's runners are blue.** The «Club member», «Club runner» and «Member bib» cells take the club's pale blue when the «Club runner» cell says «Da», by a rule with a higher priority than the status tints, so on those three cells it wins and on the rest of the row the status shows. Untick the membership offline and the blue goes.

**One new column, «Club runner» («Alergător al clubului»),** «Da» or empty, right after «Club member», written from `isClubRunner` — the one predicate the footer already counts by (§787). The typed-club match (§753) cannot be written as a spreadsheet formula, so the rule and the counts read the answer from the sheet itself instead of redoing the rule; the word is «Da», never «Nu», for the reason «Club member» never says «No» (§662). **The CSV gains the same column in the same place** — the same rows, as always: every CSV column after «Club member» moved one to the right; the ones a script reads from the end did not.

**The statistics are formulas.** Every number of the «Statistici» block is a formula cell with today's number stored beside it as its cached value, and the workbook asks for a full recalculation on open (`calcPr fullCalcOnLoad`): a phone's preview or a viewer that never recalculates shows the right number, Excel and LibreOffice recount. `COUNTA` of the ids for the total; `COUNTIF` of the status column for each state; `COUNTIF` of «Club runner» for the club; `COUNTIFS` of the sex cell's words and the age's two edges (the last band open-ended) for a category, with the status or the club added for the confirmed and the club's confirmed; «Others» is the total less the club's, and «no category» is the group's count less the categories above it, so the table always adds up, per column. The ranges are absolute and stop at the last registration; the words beside the numbers stay plain text in the file's language. `statistics.ts` still computes every number itself — the cached ones and every test's expectation — and the test evaluates each formula over the sheet's own cells and compares, and edits a cell and evaluates again. The writer learned one cell kind, `"Formula"` with `cached`, and two small hooks (`liveFormulas`: the `<v>` beside the `<f>`, and `fullCalcOnLoad`); the library already writes conditional formatting and formulas, so there is no new dependency.

**An «Event» column for a file of several events — the one addition the brief did not name.** A per-event count needs something in the sheet to filter by, and the spreadsheet had no event column (the CSV has it first). A file of several events with a footer gains «Event» after «Name», the event's label as the footer's blocks carry it, and the per-event counts are `COUNTIFS` with that column; a file of one event is exactly as before. The criterion is `"=label"`, with `~` shielding a `*`, `?` or `~` in a title and the `=` stopping a title that starts with `<` or `>` being read as a comparison; two events that would share a label get a «(2)» on the second, never one count over both; a label too long for a criterion (255 characters) leaves that event's numbers plain numbers.

**A legend under the footer,** after the definitions: «Culori» / «Colours», one line per tint with its own cell carrying a plain baked fill (a key is static by nature) and the status words it stands for, one line for the club's blue, drawn from `STATUS_TINT` so a state that gains a tint gains its rule and its legend line together. In the spreadsheet only: the CSV is the same rows, no styling, no footer. A new definition sentence says the numbers and the colours follow an edit and that a row written below the last runner is not counted.

**Refused.** A baked fill on a data cell; red for a cancelled row; a second sheet or a helper column hidden to the right; making the CSV carry a legend or a footer; a new dependency; a migration (everything is on the rows already); counting the club's runners by a formula over the typed club (it cannot be written); one differential format per status (one per tint: five in all). **Not done, and said:** a category that has no row today is not listed, so an offline edit that moves a runner into a band the file has no row for lands under «No category» rather than in a new line — listing all twelve categories always would have changed the block's layout for every file; the owner may ask for it.

**Tests.** `registrations/excel-live.test.ts` reads the bytes: the differential formats, the rules' columns, words, ranges and priorities, no baked fill on a data cell, the formulas' text, every formula evaluated over the sheet's own cells against its cache, the offline edits, `fullCalcOnLoad`, the «Club runner» column in both files, the several-events column and its escapes, the legend in both languages, and the sponsor sheet untouched. The CSV snapshot moved by the one new column; the footer's tests moved where they assumed the notes were the last lines (a legend follows them now) and where they asserted the sheet held no formula (the counts are formulas now; a label's own cell still holds none).

**Consequences.** `registrations/sheet-colours.ts` (new), `statistics.ts`, `workbook.ts`, `csv.ts`, `domain/club-runner.ts`, `theme/brand.ts` (`SHEET_TINT`), the export route (the CSV's flag), `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Admin.registrations.statistics`: `note5` and `legend*`), `docs/VIBECODING.md`. The sponsor sheet (`sponsor-sheet.ts`) is unchanged and its tests pass. No migration, no dependency.
changelogLine: - **The registrations Excel, live** — a row takes a pale colour by its status (green confirmed, yellow waiting for an answer, light blue on the waiting list, grey cancelled or expired) and the club's runners' cells are blue, both following the cell if you edit it offline; the «Statistici» numbers are formulas that recount by themselves; a new «Club runner» column («Da») follows «Club member» in the Excel and the CSV, a file of several events gains an «Event» column, and a legend of the colours closes the footer. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 158. Given the registrations export in Excel, when it is downloaded, then every number of the «Statistici» block is a COUNTA, COUNTIF or COUNTIFS formula over the sheet's own columns (the id, the status, the new «Club runner» column, the sex, the age and, in a file of several events, the «Event» column) with the number computed at the time of the download stored as its cached value, and the workbook recalculates on open; the rows are coloured by conditional formatting rules (never a fill on a cell) over exactly the data rows, one tint per kind of status — confirmed, waiting for an answer, on the waiting list, ended in grey, never red — and the «Club member», «Club runner» and «Member bib» cells blue when «Club runner» says «Da», that rule outranking the tints; a legend of the colours follows the definitions, in the list's language; the «Club runner» column («Da» or empty, from the one predicate that counts the club's runners) follows «Club member» in the spreadsheet and in the CSV, which carries no legend and no footer (2026-10-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `registrations/excel-live.test.ts` and `registrations/statistics-footer.test.ts`.

batchLine: the Excel export, live: colours by status and membership as conditional formatting, the statistics as formulas
